disease_label_per_paper: Successful treatment of carbapenemase-producing pandrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia
presentation_summary: 64-year-old woman with diabetes underwent intestinal transplant after total colectomy and short bowel syndrome, with induction and maintenance immunosuppression.

Early posttransplant course included intra-abdominal collection growing carbapenemase-producing K. pneumoniae; Hodge test was positive, KPC was confirmed, and class B/D carbapenemase genes including IMP, NDM, VIM, and OXA were not detected.

On postoperative day 65 she developed recurrent fever and leukocytosis and was found to have CRKP bacteremia; central venous catheter tip and urine also grew CRKP, and central venous catheters were changed.

Blood cultures remained positive for more than 6 days despite colistin, tigecycline, and extended-infusion meropenem. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus ertapenem sterilized blood cultures within 24 hours; she completed 2 weeks and left ICU, later dying of heart failure about 1 month after treatment.
